To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) customer anxiety negatively impacts customer choice satisfaction, 2) the negative effects of customer anxiety can be mitigated by giving customers access to human contact during self service transactions, and 3) access to human contact is a powerful tool that firms can use to improve customer choice satisfaction and long term engagement.

(1) customer anxiety has a negative impact on choice satisfaction, trust, and long-term service engagement, (2) the negative effect of anxiety on choice satisfaction and trust can be mitigated by the mere availability of access to human interaction, and (3) the mere availability of the option to interact has a positive impact on long-term engagement.

(1) anxiety negatively impacts customer satisfaction with self service choices, (2) the mere availability of access to human support mitigates anxiety's negative effects, (3) access to human support increases customer acceptance of service, and (4) the negative effects of customer anxiety on customer satisfaction and firm trust are not well understood or consistently factored into self service design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the negative consequences of customer anxiety and the ways in which firms can reduce these effects by incorporating access to human contact into self service systems.
how the negative effects of customer anxiety on firm outcomes can be mitigated through the provision of access to human support.
how anxiety impacts customer satisfaction and long term service engagement, and how access to human contact mitigates these negative effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

anxiety is a significant and underappreciated force in service design and management and that giving anxious customers access to human contact is one effective means to mitigate the negative effects of their anxiety.
access to human interaction is a powerful antidote to the negative effects of customer anxiety on choice satisfaction and firm trust.
access to human support can mitigate the negative effects of customer anxiety on choice satisfaction, firm satisfaction, and trust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anxiety is an important factor to consider when designing self service technology.
access to human interaction is an important tool for managing customer anxiety, which can be achieved by offering customers the option to interact, even if few actually choose to take it up.
the negative effects of customer anxiety on choice satisfaction and firm trust are mediated by access to human contact, even when the contact is not actually used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anxiety has negative effects on service relationships, and that access to human interaction can mitigate these effects.
companies should not ignore the role that customer anxiety plays in service relationships, nor assume that self service is the only way to reduce the costs of service provision.
the negative effects of customer anxiety on firm trust and long term engagement can be mitigated by giving customers access to human contact, even if they do not choose to use it.
